title: engineered-swarm-harness-for-deterministic-throughput-certification-and-customer-validation
creator: Ava Kim
description: Build a deterministic, tenant-aware swarm load harness and benchmarking methodology for certifying Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees and customer acceptance. The harness must be able to reproduce customer QPS/QPS-per-tenant mixes, drive autoscaler policies, validate tail-latency SLOs under warm/cold KV cache scenarios, validate model fallback and quantized model variants, and produce a customer-facing evidence bundle for acceptance signoff. This ticket covers design, implementation, standard experiment catalog, reporting dashboard integrations, and the customer acceptance checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can replay a recorded tenant mix and reproduce 95th/99th percentile latency within ±7% across 10 runs
End-to-end experiment includes warm-cache and cold-cache profiles and reports separate metrics
Autoscaler policy tests verify cooldown and scale-up thresholds; no tenant-facing errors during policy transitions in 99% of runs
Evidence bundle generated per run containing: run config, seed, telemetry snapshot, GitHub PR link, and signed acceptance checklist
Customer acceptance playbook is documented and validated with at least one pilot customer (internal or external)
tasks: Design harness architecture: orchestrator, tenant-mixer, request-replayer, verifier (Ava)
Implement deterministic load driver with RNG seed and replay fidelity controls (Diego)
Integrate autoscaler stimulation harness to exercise scale-up/scale-down policies (SRE)
Add KV prefix warmup/teardown scenarios and measure impact on token-per-second (TP/S)
Build regression-aware metrics exporter with run tagging for per-model and per-quantization variant
Create customer evidence bundle generator and template for acceptance signoff
Add dashboard panels in Console for run comparisons and golden baseline overlays
Pilot run with internal staging tenant and iterate on acceptance criteria
test_plan: Baseline run: single-model, single-tenant QPS ramp to steady-state hold (5m), record 50 runs
Tenant-mix replay: 20-tenant profile with Pareto traffic distribution; compare 95/99 latency against baseline
Autoscaler stress: simulate sudden 3x QPS spike and sustained 2x for 10m to validate scale and cooldown
Cold-cache stress: purge KV caches pre-run and measure cold start token throughput
Model-variant smoke: run same workload against fp16, int8-quantized, and fallback model to measure degradation and cost delta
Determinism verification: rerun same seed ten times and calculate coefficient of variation for key metrics
metrics: latency_p50_p95_p99_ms: latency quantiles per model and route
success_rate: 2xx responses as fraction of total requests
tokens_per_second: effective token throughput across workers
autoscaler_actions: timestamps and reason for scale events
cpu_gpu_utilization: per-node resource utilization during run
kv_cache_hit_rate: prefix KV hits vs misses
runbook: Provision dedicated staging pool with same SKU mix as customer target
Upload tenant-mix profile to harness and lock seed value for determinism
Run baseline ramp to steady state; capture telemetry snapshot link
Execute autoscaler stress profile and observe scale events in Console; annotate any unexpected errors
Generate evidence bundle and upload to customer-facing Drive folder
If run fails acceptance criteria, attach debug traces, core dumps, and rerun after mitigation
notes: We intentionally decoupled tenant-mixer from request generator so customers can supply recorded traffic samples or synthetic distributions.
Deterministic RNG seed + fixed scheduling of header metadata proved necessary in an earlier prototype to reduce run noise.
SRE recommended capturing pre-run node health snapshot to correlate transient infra noise with outlier runs.
